claim_boundary: The observatory describes task pressure, adoption and labour-market evidence at their published grain. It does not estimate occupation-level job loss, employment growth or a Jevons effect.

causal_model.outcome_identity: labour outcome = displacement + productivity and scale + new tasks + composition + adjustment

mechanisms.question: Can AI substitute for labour in tasks that workers currently perform?
mechanisms.v9_evidence: Detailed task pressure is available for 987 occupations.

mechanisms.question: Do lower costs, lower prices or better quality expand demand enough to offset labour savings?
mechanisms.v9_evidence: National firm-adoption and self-reported productivity context is available.

mechanisms.question: Does AI create new products or tasks where people retain comparative advantage?
mechanisms.v9_evidence: MOM reports aggregate creation of AI-related roles among some adopting firms.
missing_for_outcome: evidence that new work reaches displaced workers

mechanisms.question: Does AI raise the value of human judgment, accountability, relationships or physical execution?
mechanisms.v9_evidence: Mapped tasks and reviewed guidance are available; a validated occupation measure is not.

mechanisms.question: Will firms adopt the technology and redesign production around it?
mechanisms.v9_evidence: National, firm-size and selected sector adoption evidence is available.
missing_for_outcome: workflow and team redesign by occupation

mechanisms.question: Who gains, who bears adjustment costs and how do workers move or retrain?
mechanisms.v9_evidence: Broad age, sex, work-arrangement, vacancy and re-entry context is available.

causal_model.scenario_policy: No contraction, expansion, complementarity, slow-diffusion or polarisation scenario is assigned without compatible evidence on adoption, market response and labour outcomes.

ai_adoption.scope: Private sector establishments with at least 10 employees.
ai_adoption.notes: MOM reports AI adoption remains early and uneven, with no indication of significant job displacement at this point. The metrics are used as contextual adoption evidence, not as occupation-level realised displacement data.

vacancy_update.title: Written Answer to PQ on Trends in Job Vacancies
vacancy_update.vacancy_change_context: The decline in vacancies was mainly in non-PMET roles.
vacancy_update.ai_response_population: Firms that had adopted AI; about three in ten firms had adopted AI at the time of the cited survey.
vacancy_update.rounding: Employment-response percentages are rounded values reported in the parliamentary answer.
limitations: The vacancy totals are national and cannot be assigned to detailed SSOC occupations.
The firm responses are reported among AI-adopting firms and do not identify AI's causal effect on employment.
Entry-level PMET openings use the source definition and are not a complete measure of outcomes for first-time jobseekers.

labour_market_q2_advance.limitation: Advance macro figures only. Q1 2026 remains the latest detailed occupation-group release until the full Q2 report.

source.title: Labour Force in Singapore 2025, advance release

early_career.population: Singapore residents aged 15 to 29 with previous work experience
early_career.classification: Unemployed residents are classified by their previous occupation as PMET or non-PMET.
limitations: Excludes unemployed residents without work experience, including many never-employed fresh entrants.
The denominator is employed residents plus unemployed residents who previously worked in the occupation class.
These are not total youth-unemployment rates and do not identify an AI effect.
National, firm-size and sector observations cannot be assigned to a detailed occupation.
Employer responses are descriptive and may overlap; they do not identify a causal AI effect.
Advance quarterly figures are preliminary and use a different grain from annual detailed sources.

publication_gates.detailed_adoption: Requires occupation-linked adoption observations with a stated sampling frame and period.
publication_gates.productivity_scale: Requires compatible price, quantity or revenue evidence and a demand-response design.
publication_gates.new_tasks: Requires versioned occupation or task observations showing genuinely new human work.
publication_gates.job_quality: Requires hours, intensity, autonomy, monitoring or contract evidence at compatible grain.
publication_gates.causal_outcomes: Requires adoption timing, a defensible comparison group and outcome data at compatible grain.
publication_gates.transitions: Requires observed Singapore mobility and training outcomes rather than structural similarity alone.
publication_gates.longitudinal_pressure: Requires a second methodologically comparable V9 task-pressure snapshot.
